headline: OpenAI releases AI-generated mathematical research claims with specialist-led review groups
summary: On October 26, 2026, OpenAI announced three AI-generated research claims spanning harmonic analysis, computational complexity and quantum field theory, and described external expert-led groups to examine them. OpenAI says it publicly released manuscripts and Lean formalizations for local smoothing and an ETH refutation; a separate physics claim remains without public AI-produced artifacts. The official formalization catalog maps local-smoothing declarations to a Lean source file whose proof bodies invoke existing development theorems, and maps the ETH exact-counting theorem to a separate source file with a completed proof body. The linked ComparatorChallenges files contain `sorry` placeholders, but the repository instructions identify them as challenge configurations, so those placeholders alone do not refute formal proof coverage. This activation did not pin the repository revision, run Lean, audit dependencies or axioms, establish complete manuscript-to-formal correspondence, or obtain independent mathematical review. The theorem results therefore remain source-attributed claims with correctness, novelty and community acceptance unresolved.
